sources.cite: AWS documentation, How AWS Transit Gateway works, and Transit gateway route tables
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. 'You can associate a transit gateway attachment with a single route table'; 'An attachment can propagate its routes to one or more route tables'; 'When you attach a VPC to a transit gateway, you must add a route to your subnet route table in order for traffic to route through the transit gateway'; the default route table is the default association and propagation table unless those are disabled. The route tables page (tgw-route-tables.html, read the same day): propagation copies an attachment's routes into a route table.

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Marlow Analytics. The new analytics VPC (10.40.0.0/16) was attached to the company transit gateway this morning. Its jobs must reach the shared-services VPC (10.10.0.0/16: Active Directory, license server, artifact cache), but every connection times out. The transit gateway was built with default association and propagation turned off; the network team uses two route tables, rt-spokes and rt-shared. The analytics platform goes live at 14:30.
handover: The attachment was created by the analytics team with a Terraform module that only creates the attachment.
Spoke VPCs associate with rt-spokes and propagate into rt-shared; shared services propagates into rt-spokes.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the analytics VPC, its transit gateway attachment, the two transit gateway route tables and the shared-services VPC.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why analytics could not reach shared services, what you changed, and how the next spoke avoids it.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The transit gateway has default association and propagation off; the Terraform module created the attachment only, so it was associated with no route table and nothing learned 10.40.0.0/16.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Associated the attachment with rt-spokes and propagated it into rt-shared; Reachability Analyzer found the path and LDAP connected. Joining rt-shared and propagating everywhere breaks segmentation; rebooting instances cannot fix a missing route.

parts.label: Next spoke
parts.modelAnswer: The module now creates the association and propagation, and onboarding runs a reachability check.

expertPath.text: No association, no propagation; no 10.40 route in rt-shared; VPC routes fine; analyzer agrees.
Associate rt-spokes; propagate rt-shared; module and onboarding check.

flattened.headline: Follow the route table design
flattened.body: Spokes associate with the spoke table and propagate into the shared table. Putting a spoke on the shared table opens spoke-to-spoke paths the design forbids.

goLivePostponed.headline: An attachment with no association routes nothing
goLivePostponed.body: With default association and propagation off, every attachment needs an explicit association and propagation.

routed.headline: Good: association and propagation, per the design
routed.body: You read the attachment and both route tables, confirmed the VPC side, associated with rt-spokes and propagated into rt-shared, verified with Reachability Analyzer, and fixed the module.

scoring.modelReasoning: With default association and propagation off, a new attachment does nothing until told: this one has no association and no propagation, so traffic from analytics has no table and shared services has no route back. Follow the design: associate with rt-spokes and propagate into rt-shared, then verify with Reachability Analyzer. Joining the shared table opens spoke-to-spoke paths; rebooting instances cannot fix routing. Then fix the module and add a reachability check to onboarding.
